reference: No GNU/POSIX clip command exists, and stock GNU Bash lacks the required buf API, so these are documented-contract cases rather than GNU parity cases. Fixed stdout expectations are derived from the clip/buf docs and independently encoded fixture bytes; no expected value comes from the candidate. The metadata case checks Bash type/help output. Allocation-failure atomicity is deferred because the static runner has no allocator fault hook.
coverage: Bash builtin type and help metadata
Half-open line ranges, empty line pieces, and line insertion
Cross-line byte cuts with UTF-8 and embedded NUL, then exact restoration
Byte-column behavior that splits a UTF-8 sequence
16-slot physical order, oldest-entry replacement after rotation, and wrap navigation
No-piece versus empty-piece behavior for line and column paste
Raw binary output through clip text -F
Out-of-range failures and preservation of prior ring/buffer state
Copied entry independence after source free, explicit clear, and empty-ring paste error.
exclusions: No GNU CLI provides clip's in-memory ring and buf handle operations, so runnable operations are honest contract checks, not fake command parity.
Allocator failure rollback is deferred pending a disposable fault-injection build.
The suite does not cover readonly handle destinations, handle-table exhaustion/reuse, output-device failures, randomized model sequences, large paged buffers, or editor/terminal integration.

cases.purpose: Check Bash identifies clip as a loadable builtin and help exposes its documented ring description.
cases.script:
type_name=$(type -t clip)
[[ $type_name == builtin ]]
doc=$(help clip)
case $doc in
  *'Cut/copy/paste with 16-slot yank ring'*) printf 'type=%s\nhelp=clip-ring\n' "$type_name" ;;
  *) exit 1 ;;
esac

cases.purpose: Copy a half-open line range containing an empty line, print its pieces as hex, then paste the pieces at the buffer end.
cases.script:
printf 'one\n\nthree\nfour' > input
buf new -h b
buf load "$b" input
clip new -h c
clip copy-range "$c" "$b" 1 3
printf 'entry='
clip text "$c" -X
clip paste "$c" "$b" 4
printf 'buffer='
buf text "$b" -X
clip free "$c"
buf free "$b"

cases.purpose: Cut a byte range across two lines containing UTF-8 and NUL bytes, inspect the pieces, and paste them back at the original byte column.
cases.script:
printf 'A\303\251\nB\000C\nD' > input
buf new -h b
buf load "$b" input
clip new -h c
clip cut-range "$c" "$b" 0 1 1 2
printf 'entry='
clip text "$c" -X
printf 'cut='
buf text "$b" -X
clip paste "$c" "$b" 0 1
printf 'restored='
buf text "$b" -X
clip free "$c"
buf free "$b"

cases.purpose: Confirm columns are byte offsets by cutting one byte from a two-byte UTF-8 character and restoring it exactly.
cases.script:
printf '\303\251Z' > input
buf new -h b
buf load "$b" input
clip new -h c
clip cut-range "$c" "$b" 0 1 0 2
printf 'piece='
clip text "$c" -X
printf 'cut='
buf text "$b" -X
clip paste "$c" "$b" 0 1
printf 'restored='
buf text "$b" -X
clip free "$c"
buf free "$b"

cases.purpose: Fill all 16 physical slots, rotate toward older entries, then push a new copy; verify the oldest slot is replaced and navigation wraps between newest and oldest.
cases.script:
for ((i=0; i<17; i++)); do
  if ((i > 0)); then printf '\n'; fi
  printf 'L%d' "$i"
done > input
buf new -h b
buf load "$b" input
clip new -h c
for i in {0..15}; do clip copy-line "$c" "$b" "$i"; done
clip yank-prev "$c"
clip yank-prev "$c"
clip copy-line "$c" "$b" 16
for i in {0..15}; do
  printf 'slot%s=' "$i"
  clip text "$c" -N "$i" -X
done
clip yank-prev "$c"
printf 'prev='
clip text "$c" -X
clip yank-next "$c"
printf 'next='
clip text "$c" -X
clip free "$c"
buf free "$b"

cases.purpose: Distinguish a line-range entry with no pieces from a zero-length byte range containing one empty piece: the former pastes nothing, while the latter inserts an empty line but is a column-paste no-op.
cases.script:
printf 'x\ny' > input
buf new -h b
buf load "$b" input
clip new -h c
clip copy-range "$c" "$b" 0 0
clip paste "$c" "$b" 1
printf 'no-pieces='
buf text "$b" -X
clip copy-range "$c" "$b" 0 0 0 0
printf 'empty-piece='
clip text "$c" -X
clip paste "$c" "$b" 1
printf 'line-paste='
buf text "$b" -X
clip paste "$c" "$b" 0 1
printf 'column-paste='
buf text "$b" -X
clip free "$c"
buf free "$b"

cases.purpose: Write a multi-piece entry, including an embedded NUL, through clip text -F to a relative fixture file and reload it to verify exact raw bytes.
cases.script:
printf 'ab\nc\000d' > input
buf new -h b
buf load "$b" input
clip new -h c
clip copy-range "$c" "$b" 0 2
exec 3>dump
clip text "$c" -F 3
exec 3>&-
buf new -h d
buf load "$d" dump
printf 'dump='
buf text "$d" -X
clip free "$c"
buf free "$b"
buf free "$d"

cases.purpose: Capture the documented status for an out-of-range line and reversed range, then confirm both failures leave the previous ring entry and buffer bytes unchanged.
cases.script:
printf 'a\nb' > input
buf new -h b
buf load "$b" input
clip new -h c
clip copy-line "$c" "$b" 0
if clip copy-line "$c" "$b" 9; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
printf 'bad-line=%s\n' "$rc"
if clip copy-range "$c" "$b" 1 0; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
printf 'bad-range=%s\n' "$rc"
printf 'ring='
clip text "$c" -X
printf 'buffer='
buf text "$b" -X
clip free "$c"
buf free "$b"

cases.purpose: Validate the all-or-nothing buffer and ring guarantee when cut, copy, or paste allocation fails.
cases.reason: Requires a disposable build of buf and clip with a test-only allocator fault hook and an independent snapshot checker. The supplied static candidate runner exposes no allocation hook. In that environment, fail each allocation point for representative line/byte cuts, copies, and line/column pastes; verify buffer bytes, dirty state, every ring slot, and active position remain unchanged before confirming the next non-failing operation. No operation is executed in this deferred case.

cases.purpose: Copied ring entries outlive their source buffer; clearing an entry empties its bytes without freeing the ring.
cases.script:
printf 'retained bytes' > input
buf new -h b
buf load "$b" input
clip new -h c
clip copy-line "$c" "$b" 0
buf free "$b"
clip text "$c" -X
clip clear "$c"
clip text "$c" -X
clip free "$c"

cases.purpose: An empty ring cannot be pasted and reports the documented ordinary failure.
cases.script:
buf new -h b
clip new -h c
clip paste "$c" "$b" 0
